summary.text: John Braun is the Republican candidate for Washington's 3rd District. A retired Navy captain with 31 years in the submarine force and its reserve, he is president of the family-founded emergency vehicle manufacturer Braun Northwest in Chehalis. He has served in the Washington State Senate since 2013 and leads the chamber's Republican caucus. His campaign website says he is running to bring a manufacturer's discipline to Washington, D.C.

paragraphs.text: Born in Columbus, Ohio, in 1967. According to his campaign website, his father, uncle, and grandfather began building ambulances in Ohio in 1972; the family moved to Lewis County, Washington, and in 1986 his parents and their sons founded Braun Northwest in Chehalis.
Earned a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from the University of Washington in 1989 on a Naval ROTC scholarship.

Served in the U.S. Navy and Navy Reserve for 31 years, including seven years on active duty in the submarine force, rising to the rank of captain; his campaign website says his final assignment was Director of the U.S. Navy Submarine Force Reserve Component.
Earned a master's degree in manufacturing engineering and an MBA from the University of Michigan in 1999.

Returned to Braun Northwest as general manager and vice president in 1999 and became president in 2006, according to his campaign website; the company builds emergency vehicles and says it has about 350 employees.
Elected to the Washington State Senate in 2012, defeating fellow Republican incumbent Dan Swecker, and took office in January 2013 representing the 20th Legislative District.

In the Senate, he chaired the Ways and Means Committee in 2017 and, per his campaign website, helped lead the 2017-19 operating budget. In the 2023-24 session he was Vice Chair of the Rules Committee and a member of the Ways and Means, Housing, and Labor, Commerce and Tribal Affairs committees.
Elected leader of the Senate Republican caucus by his colleagues in December 2020, per his campaign website, and re-elected to the post in 2024.
Announced his campaign for the 3rd District seat in August 2025. According to his campaign website, he lives on a farm in rural Lewis County with his wife, Marlo, and has four adult children.
